notes:
Lead profile: early-stage SMB focused on automating support workflows. Inbound came from blog post about 'structured ticket summaries' + hosted API signup. Currently on free tier; already prototyped a webhook from Zendesk to Redwood test key.

Discovery highlights:
- Primary workloads: ticket summarization (one-pager), automated actions via tool-calling (e.g., update ticket status, add internal note), structured JSON outputs for downstream automation.
- Latency/throughput: small team, latency-sensitive for agent assist. Target p50 generation latency 150-300ms, can accept higher p95 during peaks. Expected steady-state ~2000-5000 tokens/day, peaks up to ~50k tokens on sale days. Cost-sensitive; wants cost visibility and token-level billing.
- Model prefs: prefers smaller efficient open models or Redwood-verified low-latency variants. Will consider quantized model variants. Not tied to a single model vendor.
- Security: needs SSO/SAML for console, audit logs for actions, and retention controls (90-day retention target). Data residency not strict today but flagged as a future requirement. Asking for SOC2 or equivalent; asked about KMS for later.
- Integration needs: Zendesk + Intercom; wants examples for tool-calling patterns (approve/close ticket, reassign) and JSON schema outputs to wire into downstream rules engine.

Quotes/rep notes:
- "We want predictable cost otherwise finance won't sign off." — Head of Ops
- "If we can auto-close low-risk tickets and attach structured summaries to the CRM, that's a 30% agent time win." — CTO

POC ask: one-week POC with hosted API keys, example tool-calling templates, and a templated structured-output schema for ticket-summary that includes fields: summary, root_cause, recommended_action, severity (low/med/high), suggested_route (self-serve/article/escalate).

Next steps/risks: Schedule SE demo (Priya) w/ engineering on 2026-03-05. Risk: SOC2 request may push to procurement if must have before POC. Budget: small ARR expected first year ($5k-$20k).
